controlConfig.name: info-1
controlConfig.text:
Responsive design means that a web HMI automatically adapts to different display sizes, resolutions and orientations. This behavior can be achieved with WebIQ using the following approaches, which we will present in this demo:
- using Layout Containers
- layouting with tiles
- using flexible widgets
- letting widgets flow into layout
- hiding information
- using scrolling

controlConfig.name: info-2
controlConfig.text: We demonstrate the approaches with a small sample HMI. Take a look at it step by step from top to bottom. We have highlighted the important elements for the corresponding step in magenta.

controlConfig.name: info-3
controlConfig.text: On the top right, you will find an info icon for each step. Click on it and you will receive additional information about each step.

controlConfig.name: iq-text
controlConfig.text: Responsive behavior doesn't happen automatically. You need to define the layout for typical target screens before creating the HMI. Do some scribbles or wireframes in order to describe the responsive behavior.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: The underlying magic for Responsive Design with WebIQ is the Layout Containers. Break down the layout into rough areas, which you devide into further sub-areas. You can recreate these areas with layout containers.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_2
controlConfig.text: At first you need some practice, but soon you can do it blindfolded.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_3
controlConfig.text: Here you can find the layout containers for our small example HMI.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_4
controlConfig.text: For more info: Layout Demo + Designer Manual, Chapter "6. Layouting Your HMI With Containers"

controlConfig.name: iq-text
controlConfig.text: For Responsive Design, it is easier if you design your HMI layout with tiles. The tiles can be placed on the screen like a board game. For a dynamic layout, you can move them around the screen like wooden boxes.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: In this example, the process parameter groups are designed as tiles. These contain the settings for elements from the Process Image. The reference between process parameter groups and an element in the process screen is established via the number instead of the positioning of the process parameters close to the corresponding elements. Thus, the tiles with the process parameter groups can be placed freely in the available space.

controlConfig.name: iq-text
controlConfig.text: WebIQ widgets are flexible, meaning they can either have a fixed height and/or width, or they can flexibly fit into the available space. This intelligent scaling behavior was introduced with the IQ Widgets, which are marked with the IQ indicator.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: In the present example, some widgets are highlighted that are configured to flexibly fit into the available space, such as the HMI header, the start/stop buttons or the menu.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_2
controlConfig.text:
Of course, every IQ widget also has a minimum size. But some widgets have an additional intelligent responsive behavior built in when the space gets very small:
- one-line texts are abbreviated with three dots in case of text overflow (ellipsis).
- multiline texts wrap automatically (wrapping)
- menu switches between full display and mobile view (burger menu) 

Figure it out by resizing the HMI and watch the behavior of the marked widgets.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_4
controlConfig.text: For more info: Designer Manual, Chapter "5. Description of WebIQ Widgets" + "6.3.4. Grow / Shrink"

controlConfig.name: iq-text
controlConfig.text: By default, a layout container tries to fit all widgets in one row (horizontal layout mode) or column (vertical layout mode). You can change this and have the widgets wrap as needed by using the "wrap"-option. In this case, when the end of the row (or column) is reached, a new row (or column) is opened. The widgets "wrap" at the end of the line / column.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: This means that the widgets can flow into the layout container, depending on what width or height it offers. This is a very efficient measure for realizing Responsive Design, especially if you are working with tiles for the HMI layout.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_2
controlConfig.text: Figure it out by resizing the HMI and watch the warpping of the widgets into the marked horizontal layout container.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_3
controlConfig.text: For more info: Designer Manual, Chapter "6.3.5. Wrapping"

controlConfig.text: It makes sense for small screen sizes that you hide certain information or even functions in the HMI so that the rest of the HMI can be displayed. WebIQ offers device-specific styling options for this purpose.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: When you reduce the screen size in the HMI example, you can see that the selected information / functions (logo, logout icon, process image on the left) are hidden step by step. For this we used the device-specific styling option "visisbility".

controlConfig.name: iq-text_2
controlConfig.text: Try it and reduce the screen size. If you pay close attention, you will notice that even more information is hidden. Have you found them?

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: By adding the predefined UI Action "trend-export" to a button and specifying the name of the trend group which you want to export data from, you allow the user of the HMI to export recorded data easily.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: When the HMI user clicks on that button, a dialog will be shown that allows him to select the start and end date to be used for the export.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: The exported data will be downloaded as a JSON file which will contain the data for all trend items from the trend group selected in the UI Action.

controlConfig.name: iq-text_1
controlConfig.text: The exported data will be in JSON format. To convert the JSON data to a CSV file you can for example use the free tool provided by Smart-HMI that you can download here - please note that this requires free access to the customer area:

controlConfig.name: html
controlConfig.html: Download Trend JSON To CSV Converter Tool

controlConfig.name: text-2
controlConfig.text: With the Trend widget and the Trend Select widget you only have two options to show different configurations:

controlConfig.name: text-3
controlConfig.text: 1. Predefine a set of trend curves to show in the Trend widget – if you want to show multiple different configurations of the trend data you can create e.g. a screen that contains multiple preconfigured trend sets in seperate Trend widget instances

controlConfig.name: text-4
controlConfig.text: 2. Allow the user to select different trend curves through the Trend Select widget – only a single set can be stored though automatically through Trend widget configuration

controlConfig.name: text-5
controlConfig.text:
What was missing was an option to predefine several trend sets, i.e. a configuration of different trend curves to show at the same time from all of the recorded values that are aggregated in a trend through the server backend.

Finally WebIQ 2.14 brings a great solution for this: trend sets! Trend sets allow you to configure several trend sets, i.e. combinations of trend curves from a single trend that you can predefine in WebIQ Designer for your HMI as read-only trend sets. These allow the user to pick one of the trend sets for display in the new IQ Trend Set widget.

controlConfig.name: text-6
controlConfig.text: However, this release also delivers a range of new UI Actions that you can attach to buttons and similar widgets to perform these actions:

controlConfig.name: text-7
controlConfig.text:
- create a new custom trend set based on the currently selelected trend curves (trend-set-create)
- rename an existing custom trend set (trend-set-rename)
- update an existing custom trend set (trend-set-save)
- delete an existing custom trend set (trend-set-delete)
- display a custom preconfigured trend-set on-the-fly (trend-set-values)

controlConfig.name: text-8
controlConfig.text:
There are two different locations for storing custom trend sets:

The current browser (local storage) – the same for all HMI users
The currently logged in user (user data) – different for each HMI user
With these functionalities we hope to enrich your HMI with new features your users will surely like.

controlConfig.name: t_2
controlConfig.text: This demo shows how to configure a trend recorder and how to use the trend widgets to display the recorded trend values over time.

controlConfig.name: t_4
controlConfig.text: Select the desired Trend in the navigation on the left. The Trend shows the trend curves of various values. The Trend is in live mode, i.e. new values are added to the right while the curves continuously move out to the left.

controlConfig.name: t_5
controlConfig.text: You can swipe to the right to view values from the past. With the icons in the upper right corner you can change the displayed time range. Use the pinch gesture to zoom into the trend curves. If you press the play icon, the trend display jumps back to the live mode.

controlConfig.name: t_6
controlConfig.text: Click in the trend area to display a trend handle. Click on the legend to highlight a curve. Use the setting icon to show the slide-in for selecting the other trend values.

controlConfig.name: t_7
controlConfig.text: How did we realize it? You can download the demo from the download area, load it into the  WebIQ Designer and see with which widgets and settings we created the demo.
